Roles I am open to

Get in touch →
  • 01

    Software Engineer

    Senior to Principal. Backend, platform, and product engineering in Go, Python, TypeScript, and Rust.

    Built Atlas, which seats nearly 2,000 people across three countries, and cut its page loads from 15–20 API calls to one or two.

  • 02

    Data Engineer

    Pipelines and data platforms for data too large or too messy for off-the-shelf tools.

    Built pipelines that moved 40B+ records, with streaming, encoding recovery, and schema normalisation across SQL, JSON, CSV, and XML.

  • 03

    DevOps Engineer

    Cloud infrastructure, CI/CD, and the automation that keeps deploys boring.

    Operated a four-region AWS platform of 37 ECS services and 50+ repositories, with the deployment, inventory, and alerting automation around it.

  • 04

    Threat Intelligence Analyst

    Advisories, attack surface, and email security, backed by tools I write.

    Sentinel matches GHSA, OSV, NVD, and CISA KEV against every SBOM and surfaced 5,000+ findings; domainwatch, spoofscore, and dmarc-ready show what attackers see.

  • 05

    AI systems engineer

    Agents, retrieval, and evals that hold up in production.

    Rumi narrows 4,600 postings a day to a shortlist for under a dollar a run. Now building a public benchmark of agentic software-engineering tasks.

  • 06

    Founding or early engineer

    Security, data, or AI teams going from zero to one.

    Founding Engineer at TraceGraph, CEO of Vectra Dynamics, and CTO of Optimeer Labs.

How I think

The bookshelf →
  1. 01

    Turn repeated work into a platform

    When a team does the same thing for the third time, I build the system, automation, or check that does it for them.

    From The Pragmatic Programmer

  2. 02

    Design for how data is read

    Reliability and speed come from the shape of the data and its access paths. Atlas got fast when the API matched the screen, not the tables.

    From Designing Data-Intensive Applications

  3. 03

    Every claim links to evidence

    A number, an incident, or a verdict should trace back to the record it came from, so anyone can check it. TraceGraph and Rumi are both built on that.

    From Hoare, An Axiomatic Basis for Computer Programming
